title: Evals sync 1:1 prep - regression triage + A/B notes
content:
Purpose: quick prep for 1:1 with Ravi (weekly evals sync). Focus: recent quality regression on small quantized model, results from A/B run, and immediate mitigation steps we can test this week.

Topline summary (what to say in the meeting):
- Noticed a regression starting around 2026-03-04 on the gptx-3b-q4 profile: held-back precision on classification tasks (intent categorization) — win-rate down ~7% vs baseline.
- A/B run (A=baseline model v2026-02-22, B=current v2026-03-05): B had higher hallucination vs named-entity slot extraction (F1 -5.8), slightly faster avg latency (-12ms) and token cost lower by ~8% (quantization wins).
- Hypothesis: quantization + optimized attention kernel selection under longer prefix inputs is causing subtle token order differences that bubble into decoding decisions for borderline cases. Might also be prompt-set drift (recent prompt canonicalization change on 3/2).

Quick numbers to have ready:
- Sample size: A=4.1k eval queries, B=4.0k.
- Metric deltas: intent-win-rate: A 83.1% -> B 75.7% (delta -7.4).
- NER F1: A 0.912 -> B 0.854 (delta -0.058).
- Average latency (p50): A 112ms -> B 100ms.
- Token-cost per call: A 18.4 -> B 16.9 tokens.

Short agenda for 1:1 (15 min):
1) 3-min recap of A/B deltas
2) 5-min triage of likely causes & data to fetch
3) 5-min decision on immediate mitigations (rollback vs param fixes)
4) 2-min assign action items + owners

Notes-to-self / topics to raise if time:
- Check whether recent prompt canonicalization PR (PR#142) replaced a few example templates — could have changed context-window semantics for few test cases.
- Ask infra: were there any kernel/runtime changes rolled to q4 runtime around 3/3-3/5? (SRE / release-eng).
- Confirm whether KV-cache TTL behavior changed in dedicated pools (we saw more cold-starts in the traces).

Initial hypotheses ranked:
1) Prompt rewrite on 3/2 introduced formatting that interacts poorly with quantized attention -> decoding differences.
2) Kernel selection change favors speed quantizations that lose subtle logits discrimination.
3) Evaluation dataset shifted: a small subset of edge-case queries added on 3/1 that model B handles worse.

Immediate small experiments to run this week (quick, able to get results in <48h):
- E1: Re-run failing eval subset with baseline model artifact pinned but with current prompting (isolate prompt effect). (Owner: Avery; due: 2026-03-13)
- E2: Re-run full A/B but force decoder/quant flags to baseline config on the new binary (isolate runtime/quant flag effect). (Owner: Ravi; due: 2026-03-13)
- E3: Short replay of sampled failing calls with KV cache warm (warm-run) vs cold-run to see delta. (Owner: Leah; due: 2026-03-14)

If experiments confirm quick cause -> mitigation options:
- If prompt rewrite is culprit: patch canonicalization to preserve previous delimiters for 2-week canary; push prompt compatibility fix; update docs.
- If kernel/quantization flags: roll back flag in Dedicated canary pool; schedule hotfix release for q4 runtimes.
- If dataset drift: revert dataset subset and open ticket for human review of edge cases.

Follow-ups and longer-term items (tracking):
- Run an eval-sensitivity matrix: for each prompt-template variant (old/new/trimmed), measure delta across top 10 tasks. (Owner: Avery, collaborate with Eval infra).
- Add targeted regression tests into PR gating for prompt-canonicalization PRs (small harness that checks top-5 tasks). (Owner: Ravi).
- Add a model-behavior diff tool: sample n=200 failure cases and surface token-level logits diffs to help triage decoding divergences. (Owner: Leah; note as a product / infra investment).

Action items (from this doc, to mention in meeting):
- Avery: run E1 and collect failure buckets + 10 representative examples (due 3/13).
- Ravi: run E2 with pinned flags + share config diff + timeline of when flags were promoted (due 3/13).
- Leah: run E3 and pull traces showing KV cache hit-rate by request id (due 3/14).
- Me (Avery) follow-up: if E1 points to prompt drift, draft rollback/compat patch and sync w/ DevEx to gate. (due 3/15)

Questions to ask in meeting (short):
- Ravi: do we have a quick way to force baseline kernels into canary pool without full rollback?
- Leah: can you get traces for the 150 top-failure request ids (we need token-level timing).
- PM/owner (if present): any recent product-side prompt/template rollout we should know about?

Scratch ideas (brainstorm, not committed):
- Add an automated prompt-stability score to Optimize that flags when a prompt change causes >X% model-behavior variance across pinned artifacts.
- Lightweight heuristic: when quantization reduces token-cost by >5% but F1 drops >3%, block auto-rollout.

Misc notes / references:
- Quick links: EVAL-88 dashboard (linked above), reproducer PR #142, perf traces in infra/traces/2026-03-05.
- Keep the tone: we want fast mitigation, minimal customer impact; prefer temporary prompt rollback over blocking quant gains unless customer-facing regression.

Notes to self after meeting (placeholder):
- Capture owner agreement on rollback threshold and confirm who will execute rollback in Dedicated pools.
- If we decide to patch prompt-canonicalization, include a short eval harness in the PR to avoid repeat.

End of prep. Save and bring a quick 1-slide summary if asked (I will screenshot the numbers above).
